name: Glassmorphism. The label was normalized from a frosted-glass interface description, so it is not a canonical definition. Category: Digital and 3D Aesthetics.
visualIdentity: Explicit: translucent frosted panels with thin borders, soft shadows, and restrained highlights. The background color shows through the panels without lowering text contrast. Excessive layers of blur should be avoided. Negative examples in the source are not positive evidence.
suitableUses: Explicit good fits: editorial narratives, product explainers, document or process sequences, and flat vector, collage, sticker, or motion-poster layouts. Explicit: simple layered UI cards over color. Inferred: app feature demos, SaaS onboarding, and analytics dashboards, based on the listed combinations.
limitations: Explicit: avoid blur on blur, and avoid low-contrast white text. Adapt or omit the style when the stack hides content viewers must read, when overlap obscures provenance or comparison labels, or when the style requires fixed print geometry. Blur behavior must be inspected in the target rendering browser.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #182837, foreground #F6F7F0, accent_1 #7AAEB4, accent_2 #A698C5. Task-provided or approved colors override these. Opaque checks give foreground on background 13.94:1, and background-colored text on accent_1 6.112:1 and accent_2 5.666:1. An optional LAB gradient from accent_1 to accent_2 may sit only behind the glass. Opaque ratios do not validate translucent panels, so frames must be rechecked.
motionAndInteraction: Explicit: panels, masks, and modest parallax animate, with glass treatments kept restrained. Shared movement guidance applies, so deliberate cuts and reading holds are preserved. Motion references are optional and unmandated; candidates include card stacking, pointer tilt, chapter transitions, swipe carousels, and scroll storytelling, each requiring compatibility screening. Video must derive state from composition time, while live hover or scroll belongs only to interactive delivery.
audio: Unspecified in the source. The style mandates no music, voiceover, sung vocals, or effects. Any audio choice should be inferred from topic, audience, objective, and motion, and honor explicit requirements first. Inferred: restrained ambience or subtle accents may suit soft glass transitions. Any speech must stay intelligible and must not compete with essential text.
assetRequirements: Unspecified in the source; no required assets are listed. Practical inputs include exact copy, subject assets, the palette or an approved reference, and local fonts loaded before rendering. Inferred: the frosted effect needs colorful or textured content behind the panels to read as glass. Any missing asset must be stated. A PhotoSwipe lightbox is conditional on an interactive image gallery only.
combinations: Explicit: style-095 (product motion for state transitions, shared-element motion, and feedback timing) suits app feature demos and SaaS onboarding. Explicit: style-097 (charts inside panels) suits analytics dashboards. Rules: at most two stacked blur layers, text checked against the worst-case background, gradients only behind glass, and charts on a more opaque fill. Avoid pairing with other translucent or aurora styles.
productionApproach: Explicit: HTML/CSS (backdrop-filter, clip-path) and SVG act as style renderers for the visuals. Motion may use GSAP (paused, seekable timeline) or Motion as optional engines, with one owner per animated property. HyperFrames is the default pipeline for composition, sync, validation, and export. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists, and the reason must be recorded. chroma.js validates colors and contrast. Delivery checks include decoded frames, audio sync, and loop seams. Simulated appearance must be distinguished from photographed production.
